intended_object: The kernel f⁻¹(false) of a bounded lattice homomorphism f : A → Bool (the two-element lattice), viewed as an order ideal of A; this is the prime ideal corresponding to f in the standard correspondence between prime ideals and homomorphisms to 2 (from the docstring and module doc).
explanation: The carrier is {a | f a = false}, the preimage of ⊥. It is nonempty (f ⊥ = false), closed under joins (f(a ⊔ b) = f a || f b = false) and a lower set (f is monotone), so it is the correct order ideal. No degenerate case fails: if A is a one-point lattice, no bounded homomorphism to Bool exists. The construction itself only uses that f preserves ⊔ and ⊥, but the module's goal is the bijection between prime ideals and bounded lattice homomorphisms to Bool (primeEquivBoolHom). That bijection needs ⊓ and ⊤ to be preserved, so bounded lattice homomorphisms on a lattice with ⊥ and ⊤ is the standard setting. Mathlib has Order.Ideal.IsPrime and PrimePair, but I found no construction of an ideal from a Bool-valued homomorphism.
